links.comparator_used: Alternative persona components: lean-efficiency optimization target (versus safety-first), and high versus low time-pressure framing. There was no no-persona arm.
links.outcome: Safety-net specificity in discharge plans and contraindication or sequencing violations in trap cases
links.effect: Safety-first improved safety-net specificity (mean 4.5 versus 2.6 on a five-point scale). Violations occurred only in the high/lean condition (8 of 56 runs, 14.3%). In trap cases, violations were 8 of 8 under high/lean and 0 of 24 in the other three conditions. Safety-first also increased proposed testing (beta = 1.32, p < 0.001) and diagnostic breadth (beta = 0.247, p < 0.001). High time pressure reduced proposed tests (beta = -1.05, p < 0.001) and diagnostic breadth (beta = -0.246, p < 0.001).
links.tradeoff: Safety-first prompting increased the number of proposed tests (beta = 1.32). High time-pressure framing narrowed diagnostic search and reduced testing, and the high/lean persona produced all the violations.
links.quote: Time-pressure framing narrowed diagnostic search and reduced proposed testing, whereas safety-first prompting improved safety-netting and prevented severe trap-case violations outside the high/lean condition.
